source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text: This source's disease section names durian's four to five most significant fungal/oomycete problems, matching the entries given in more species-level detail in Source B of this batch: stem and patch canker and root rot (both caused by Phytophthora palmivora, the single most economically important durian pathogen worldwide), pink disease (fungal bark infection favored by humid, crowded canopies), Phomopsis leaf blight, and anthracnose/leaf spot affecting both leaves and fruit. This source's general management principle across all of them is consistent with Source B: good drainage and avoiding waterlogging, avoiding unnecessary wounds to bark and roots, pruning for airflow, prompt removal and destruction of infected material, and fungicide treatment of wounds and active infections; for species-level identification detail and the individual disease descriptions, see the dedicated entries sourced from Source B in this batch.
